submission.natural_language_explanation: This broad layer-0 head rests near its mean write (weak or below the line) at most tokens, usually sitting on the first-token sink or spreading attention, but fires strongly whenever the current token completes a highly predictable local bigram with the preceding token: a nominal or quantifier plus 'of' ('one of', 'two of', 'species of'; weakest when the opener is itself 'of'), a stem plus its subword piece, a number continuing a run, a catenative verb plus 'to', a verb plus its particle or preposition ('came home', 'pointed at', 'far away'), or a conventional adjective-noun or noun-verb pairing, attending near-exclusively to that trigger word. Because almost every natural sentence contains at least one such tight pair (very often just a word split into pieces), sentence peaks are usually active, and 'one' followed by another word ('one more', 'one person') is still active though weaker than 'one of'; only rare sentences whose every local transition is loose, with no 'of', numbers, commas, or split words, stay fully below the line (verified: 'She whispered softly so she would not wake the sleeping baby' peaks 0.54, 'He smiled kindly at small kids' peaks 0.63, against the 0.749 line).
